newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Malaysia '97 crude output seen down, gas up.
newsitem.headline: Malaysia '97 crude output seen down, gas up.

text.p: Malaysia's crude oil production is expected to be lower this year than in 1996, while its output of natural gas will increase, Bank Negara Malaysia said in its annual report on Friday.

Total crude output rose 1.7 percent to 715,191 barrels per day (bpd) in 1996, the central bank said. But it added that excluding condensates, the production was lower at 646,000 bpd from 663,000 bpd in 1995.

Bank Negara did not give an estimate on the current year's crude production, only saying it was expected to be lower due to slower demand and moderating world oil prices following the re-entry of Iraqi oil into the market.
It also attributed the lower production to a "national depletion policy" on mining, which calls for sustainable exploitation of mineral resources.
Output of natural gas, meanwhile, is expected to stay strong due to contractual obligations, said the report.
Net production of natural gas was estimated to have risen 20.4 percent to 3.4 billion standard cubic feet per day in 1996, due to strong demand from external and domestic consumers.
The higher gas production was due to the third train of the Malaysia Liquefied Natural Gas 2 plant becoming operational in March 1996.

At the end of last year, 13 oilfields were in operation, while national oil and gas company Petronas signed a new production sharing contract in a deepwater exploration area in the east Malaysian state of Sarawak. -- Kuala Lumpur newsroom (603-2307509)
